chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, he said:

I asked him about the sick person who becomes unconscious. He said: If it exceeds three days, then there is no make-up duty upon him. But if he was rendered unconscious for three days, then he must make up the salat (prayer) during those days.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the obligatory salat (prayer) missed during unconsciousness
key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person whose condition is being discussed
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the three-day limit that determines the ruling
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: make-up performance of an obligatory act after its time has passed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up salat (prayer) for a person who was unconscious due to illness?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the sick person who loses consciousness and misses salat (prayer). It states that if the unconsciousness extends beyond three days, no make-up is required, while if it lasts for three days, the missed prayers of those days must be made up.
